clue.text: Entertainment venue close to bath full of chlorine

parts.note: nigh is an old word for near or close

indicators.note: the bath is filled with the chemical symbol, so it goes inside

parts.note: a tub is a bath
Cl is the chemical symbol for chlorine

explanation.surface: A swimming pool, perhaps, sits beside a fun venue, its water heavily chlorinated.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightclub is a place for late-night dancing and drinking, a kind of entertainment venue.

clue.text: Chart-topper set cut unmusical sound

parts.note: a chart-topper is a number one, written NO 1, with the figure 1 read as the letter I

indicators.note: cut means the word set loses its last letter

parts.note: taken as written before the cut

explanation.surface: A band's number-one song has its set shortened, leaving a tuneless racket.
explanation.walkthrough: NO 1 gives NOI, and SET cut short gives SE.
explanation.definitionFit: Noise is any sound lacking harmony or musical quality, especially a loud or unpleasant one.

clue.text: Large waves swamping tips of pontoon anchor

indicators.note: swamping means the rearranged letters surround the tips
waves means the letters of Large are tossed about into a new order
the tips are the first and last letters of pontoon

explanation.surface: Big waves wash over the ends of a floating pontoon.
explanation.definitionFit: A grapnel is a small anchor with several flukes, used for small boats or dragging.

clue.text: Handle subject of diplomatic negotiations but not completely

indicators.note: not completely means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a treaty is what diplomats negotiate

explanation.surface: Diplomats deal with the topic of their talks, but only partly.
explanation.definitionFit: To treat a matter is to deal with or handle it, as in to treat a subject carefully.

clue.text: Give away rental properties before impertinent speech

indicators.note: before places the properties ahead of the speech

parts.note: lets are properties rented out
lip is cheeky talk

explanation.surface: A landlord hands over rented homes ahead of some cheeky remarks.
explanation.definitionFit: To let slip is to reveal a secret by accident, the same as giving it away.

clue.text: Get on with climbing fell — location of high-level discussion?

indicators.note: with joins the two parts side by side

parts.note: to board a bus or train is to get on it

indicators.note: in a down clue, climbing means the word for fell is read from the bottom up

parts.note: a fell is upland moor, in northern English usage

explanation.surface: Hillwalkers press on up the fell, apparently somewhere lofty talks happen.
explanation.walkthrough: A fell in northern England is a stretch of high moorland; MOOR reads upwards as ROOM.
explanation.definitionFit: A boardroom is where a company's directors meet, so senior-level talks take place there; 'high-level' puns on height.

clue.text: Milk? Fail to provide enough, nicking quarter of pint

indicators.note: nicking means stealing, so a letter is taken away

parts.note: to skimp is to be stingy, failing to supply enough

indicators.note: pint has four letters, so a quarter of it is one letter, its first

explanation.surface: A milkman cheats customers, pinching a bit of each pint.
explanation.walkthrough: SKIMP with its P taken away leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To skim milk is to remove the cream, and skimmed milk is called skim; the question mark flags the verb or adjective sense.

clue.text: Only accepting half of UK invested in pound? That can be sorted out

indicators.note: accepting means the word for only takes the other part inside it

parts.note: sole means only, as in sole survivor

indicators.note: invested in means the letter goes inside the pound abbreviation

parts.note: lb is the abbreviation for a pound weight

indicators.note: half of the two-letter UK is its first letter

explanation.surface: A financial question about only part of Britain being invested in sterling, and whether it can be fixed.
explanation.definitionFit: A soluble problem is one that can be solved or resolved, the sense of being sorted out.

clue.text: I'm the writer with a writer's complaint, say, working in complete absorption

parts.note: taken as written without the apostrophe
the writer is the setter speaking of themselves, so me
RSI, repetitive strain injury, is a typical complaint of those who write a lot
on means working, as in the machine is on

explanation.surface: A setter describes themselves suffering a writer's ailment while working, utterly absorbed.
explanation.definitionFit: Immersion is deep mental involvement, being totally engrossed in something.

clue.text: Convenient to adopt unsuitable name for fibre

indicators.note: adopt means the word for convenient takes the other letters in

parts.note: fit means suitable or convenient
lame means feeble or unsatisfactory, as in a lame excuse

explanation.surface: Someone finds it handy to take on an unfitting name.
explanation.definitionFit: A filament is a slender thread or fibre, such as in a light bulb or a plant.

clue.text: A note about lake on fire

indicators.note: about means the word for note goes around the lake letter

parts.note: note means distinction or renown, as in a person of note, so fame
L is the abbreviation for lake on maps

explanation.surface: A message written about a lake, which is somehow burning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'note' looks musical but means renown here, FAME.
explanation.definitionFit: Aflame describes something burning or in flames, the same as being on fire.

clue.text: Fan chasing diminished top seed

indicators.note: chasing means the fan comes after the other part
diminished means the word for top loses its final letter

parts.note: a peak is the top of something
a nut is an enthusiast, as in a football nut

explanation.surface: A fan pursuing a top-seeded tennis player who has been knocked down a peg.
explanation.walkthrough: 'top seed' reads as a tennis phrase, but 'top' is wordplay and 'seed' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A peanut is the edible seed of a legume plant, grown underground in pods.

clue.text: Crawler identifying former president's wife

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a small spotted beetle that crawls on plants
second meaning: ... Johnson, wife of US President Lyndon Johnson

explanation.walkthrough: 'Crawler' suggests a sycophant, but it is the insect.
explanation.definitionFit: The red spotted beetle shares its name with the nickname of Claudia Johnson, First Lady in the 1960s.

clue.text: In general, lecturers rejected underground room

indicators.note: rejected means the hidden letters are turned backwards
in means the answer sits within the words that follow

explanation.surface: Lecturers as a group have been turned down, perhaps for a job.
explanation.definitionFit: A cellar is a storage room below ground level, beneath a house.

clue.text: Former figures in garden, with first couple moving back as a penance

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife

indicators.note: the first two letters of the garden word move further back in it

parts.note: topiary is the art of shrubs clipped into figures and shapes in a garden

explanation.surface: Old shaped hedges in a garden, with the leading pair shifted, as if in atonement.
explanation.walkthrough: In TOPIARY, the first couple TO moves back two places to give PIATORY.
explanation.definitionFit: Expiatory means making amends for wrongdoing, which is what a penance does.

clue.text: Timber European found below crest

indicators.note: in a down clue, below places the European under the crest

parts.note: a ridge is a crest, as of a hill
a Pole is a European, from Poland

explanation.surface: A European discovered beneath the crest of a hill.
explanation.definitionFit: A ridgepole is the horizontal beam of timber at the apex of a roof or tent.

clue.text: Involuntary response when calling to do with sound of speech

definitions.text: to do with sound of speech

indicators.note: when ties the twitch to the call, placing it after

parts.note: to phone is to call, so calling suggests phone
a tic is an involuntary twitch

explanation.surface: A nervous twitch that strikes whenever someone makes a phone call.
explanation.definitionFit: Phonetic means relating to speech sounds, as in the phonetic alphabet.

clue.text: Special constable carrying radio, pulled out every so often?

indicators.note: carrying means the abbreviations hold the other letters between them

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for constable

indicators.note: pulled out means the letters of radio are wrenched into a new order

explanation.surface: A volunteer police officer with a radio is pulled out of duty now and then.
explanation.definitionFit: Sporadic means occurring irregularly, at scattered times, rather than continuously.

clue.text: Despicable rise in attention about national costume

indicators.note: in a down clue, rise means the letters are read upwards
about means the word for attention surrounds the costume

parts.note: ear means attention, as in lend an ear
the kilt is the national dress of Scotland

explanation.surface: Interest grows in a country's traditional dress.
explanation.walkthrough: The kilt is the traditional Scottish garment; in a down light, 'rise' turns the whole build upside down.
explanation.definitionFit: Ratlike describes someone contemptible or sneaky, like a rat in its bad sense.

clue.text: Line about number turning up close to fantastic US city

indicators.note: about means the line goes around the other letters

parts.note: a cord is a line or string

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means the abbreviation is read upwards
the close of fantastic is its last letter

explanation.surface: A line of work turns up a number near an amazing American city.
explanation.walkthrough: Concord is the capital of New Hampshire, a fact many solvers outside the US will not know.
explanation.definitionFit: Concord is the state capital of New Hampshire, and also a town in Massachusetts.

clue.text: Fool in show of enjoyment backed rebellion

indicators.note: backed means the whole sequence is turned around
in means the fool sits inside the other word

parts.note: yum is an exclamation of delight at food
a nit is a fool or idiot

explanation.surface: A fool, cheering his enjoyment, supported an uprising.
explanation.definitionFit: A mutiny is an open revolt against authority, especially by sailors or soldiers.

clue.text: Head off evidence of bovine activity in most of the canal trail

indicators.note: in means the trimmed cow word goes inside
most of means the final letter is dropped

parts.note: taken as written before trimming

indicators.note: head off means the first letter is removed

parts.note: a cowpat is the dung left by a cow

explanation.surface: Cow dung spoiling most of the path along a canal.
explanation.definitionFit: A towpath runs beside a canal, used originally by horses towing barges.

clue.text: Positive articles regarding all the gods

parts.note: an and the are the indefinite and definite articles
on means regarding, as in a book on birds

explanation.surface: Upbeat pieces written concerning every deity.
explanation.definitionFit: A pantheon is the full set of gods worshipped by a people, such as the Greek pantheon.

clue.text: Spiritual range, undergoing change of direction? Rubbish

indicators.note: the compass point north swaps for south, so one direction letter replaces the other

parts.note: New Age describes a broad range of alternative spiritual beliefs

explanation.surface: A spiritual movement changes its direction, and the result is junk.
explanation.walkthrough: NEW AGE with N (north) turned to S (south) gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Sewage is waste matter carried in drains, and rubbish here is waste or filth.

clue.text: Independent blocking another newspaper displaying instrument

indicators.note: blocking means the letter stands in the middle of the paper's name

parts.note: the Star is a British newspaper, distinct from the Independent

explanation.surface: The Independent newspaper obstructs a rival paper with a musical feature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Independent' looks like the British newspaper, which 'another newspaper' plays on, but it is just I.
explanation.definitionFit: A sitar is a long-necked Indian stringed instrument, plucked like a lute.

clue.text: Ecological style of writing about to be promoted

indicators.note: promoted in a down clue means the letters move higher up the word

parts.note: a genre is a category or style of literature
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A green style of prose is set to get a boost.
explanation.walkthrough: In GENRE, RE moves up ahead of EN.
explanation.definitionFit: Green means environmentally friendly, the sense of ecological in politics.

clue.text: Male breaking in to knock off old cape

indicators.note: breaking in means the letter forces its way inside

parts.note: to do in is to kill, to knock off

explanation.surface: A man breaks in to murder someone wearing an old cloak.
explanation.definitionFit: A domino is a loose hooded cloak worn at masquerades, so a kind of cape.

clue.text: Escapes including receipts? They shouldn't really be seen

indicators.note: including means the receipts sit inside the escapes

parts.note: outs are means of escape, as in an easy out
take means takings or receipts, as in the day's take

explanation.surface: Getaways that include takings, which ought to stay out of sight.
explanation.definitionFit: Outtakes are filmed scenes cut from the final version, so never meant for viewers.

clue.text: Kind component of repeated penalty?

indicators.note: component of means only a middle part of the doubled word is kept, the rest discarded
repeated means the word penalty is set down a second time right after the first

parts.note: taken as written, then written again

explanation.surface: A puzzle about part of a penalty given more than once.
explanation.walkthrough: Write PENALTY twice: the end of one and the start of the next give penal-TY-PE-nalty.
explanation.definitionFit: A type is a kind, sort or category of thing.

clue.text: Dodgily roped in to swallow hot new painkiller

indicators.note: swallow means the rearranged letters take in the heat letter
dodgily means the letters are arranged in a shady, unreliable way

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: Someone shadily conscripted to gulp down a hot new pain reliever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' is not a second anagram signal here: it gives N, which joins the anagram pool.
explanation.definitionFit: Endorphins are natural hormones in the brain that reduce pain, the body's own painkillers.
